title: Constant chamber-size ratio follows from growth proportional to existing mass

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Constant chamber-size ratio follows from growth proportional to existing mass

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Each foraminiferal chamber bears a constant ratio of size to the next because the rate of increase at each instant is proportional to the whole existing mass of the homogeneous organism.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XII: The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The law of increase by which each chamber bears a constant ratio of magnitude to the next may be looked upon as a simple consequence of the structural uniformity or homogeneity of the organism; we have merely to suppose (as this uniformity would naturally lead us to do) that the rate of increase is at each instant proportional to the whole existing mass.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XII, “The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera”; topic “Constant ratio of chamber sizes”. Scope: chambered Foraminifera

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch12-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing scans can directly test chamber-size ratios. They cannot generally resolve whether proportional growth of homogeneous living mass caused those ratios.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate volumes of successive chambers and test for a constant multiplicative ratio, then compare that pattern with any available longitudinal biomass or growth-rate series. Constant chamber ratios support the geometric component, but only proportional instantaneous biomass growth would support the stated cause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil or museum shells lack instantaneous living mass and growth rate.

Constant ratios can arise from multiple developmental rules.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Relative chamber size through ontogeny is measurable on sectioned and scanned tests, and the fusulinid landmark file is already organized by whorl. The explanatory half of the claim equates that geometric series with mass-proportional growth of a homogeneous body, which shell outlines cannot separate from other constant-ratio mechanisms. The pattern is therefore testable on a subset of chambered forms, and the stated cause is not.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compute chamber or whorl volume ratios along individual ontogenies and test constancy against a model in which the ratio itself changes with age. A stable ratio matches the geometric pattern; it confirms growth proportional to existing mass only if protoplasmic mass is measured independently and scales with the same constant, which existing hard-part series do not provide.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Living mass at the moment each chamber is added is not in the morphometric archives.

A constant size ratio is also produced by other rules, including a fixed volume added in proportion to surface or a fixed developmental schedule.
